newsitem.title: USA: CB Financial restates '96 net downard.
newsitem.headline: CB Financial restates '96 net downard.

text.p: CB Financial Corp said Monday it increased its reserve for loan losses for the fourth quarter of 1996, causing it to restate its 1996 net income down $1.5 million, or $0.52 a share, to $5 million, or $1.79.

As a result of increased charge-offs in the indirect auto loan portfolios during the 1996 fourth quarter and anticipated future charge-offs, the company said an audit of its results determined it should increase the reserve for loan losses to $6.2 million, or one percent of loans outstanding, as of December 31, from $4.5 million.

The change resulted in a pre-tax fourth quarter charge of $1.6 million. In addition, the audit resulted in adjustments of $571,000 to other operating expenses, including depreciation on leasehold improvements and reserves for possible litigation liabilities, the company said.

CB Financial Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Brian Bell said the adjustments do not affect the previously announced proposed merger with Citizens Banking Corp, which is expected to close at the end of the second quarter.
Audited earnings for 1995 were $4.6 million, or $1.65 a share. CB Financial is a bank holding company with assets of $826.2 million.
